metrics.verdict_trigger: C3 fails for both primary estimators passing C1: plug-in KL K3=0.099 < 0.5, KSG k=10 K3=0.000560 < 0.5

ksg_k_invariance.finding: KSG CMI (sklearn mutual_info_classif, discrete_features=True) produces IDENTICAL results for k=5, k=10, and k=20 on discrete data. K3=0.000560, mi_joint=0.034413, mi_cond=0.033853 for all three k values.
ksg_k_invariance.implication: The KSG insensitivity is NOT specific to k=5 neighborhood resolution. sklearn's discrete-mode implementation appears to be invariant to the n_neighbors parameter on this discrete dataset, likely due to tie-handling in nearest-neighbor search for categorical features.

plugin_kl_smoothing_bias.explanation: With alpha=1.0 Laplace smoothing and 12 target classes, average K3 stratum size ~6 records, each (z,a) cell receives 12 pseudo-counts. Smoothing dominates ~67% of probability mass, creating positive bias of ~0.11 bits that masks the 1.52-bit true signal. Stochastic K3 (0.099) < degenerate K3 (0.109), meaning the estimator is LESS sensitive on the stochastic SPA than on the deterministic one.

permutation_test_exploratory.interpretation: Per-stratum PMI is strongly positive (1.46-1.69 bits) with p=0.0 for all 48 strata, confirming the true signal exists and is detectable by non-parametric stratum-level tests. The CMI estimators fail because they estimate a different quantity (joint MI minus conditional MI over the full state space) rather than per-stratum PMI.

REPLICATION-B-PARENT-KSG-K5.description: Replicate parent KSG k=5 results on stochastic SPA to verify reproducibility

observations: Plug-in KL estimator (alpha=1.0 Laplace) achieves K3=0.099 bits on stochastic SPA where true I(Y;A|Z)=1.52 bits. C1 passes (|null_mean|=0.064 < 0.1) but C3 fails (0.099 < 0.5). Critically, the degenerate control on deterministic SPA gives K3=0.109 > 0.099, meaning the smoothing bias exceeds the true signal — the estimator is LESS sensitive on the stochastic SPA than on the degenerate baseline.

KSG CMI produces IDENTICAL results for k=5, k=10, and k=20 on this discrete dataset: K3=0.000560, mi_joint=0.034413, mi_cond=0.033853 for all three. This confirms the KSG insensitivity is NOT specific to k=5 neighborhood resolution — sklearn's mutual_info_classif with discrete_features=True is invariant to the n_neighbors parameter on this data, likely due to tie-handling in categorical nearest-neighbor search.
All 4 estimators pass C1 (null centering works) with within-session shuffle. Plug-in KL |null_mean|=0.064, KSG |null_mean|=0.012 for all k values. The null framework is sound.

Per-stratum permutation test (exploratory) shows 48/48 strata with significant PMI (p=0.0 after Bonferroni correction). Individual stratum PMI ranges from 1.46 to 1.69 bits, consistent with the audit-confirmed true CMI of ~1.52 bits. The signal is clearly present and detectable by stratum-level tests — the CMI estimators fail because they estimate a different statistical quantity.

Stratum size decomposition: 2 non-empty buckets (5-9: 343 strata, 10-19: 37 strata). No 20-49 or 50+ strata. The stochastic SPA produces many small strata due to the high-dimensional (state, history_action_K) conditioning.
KSG k=5 replication exactly matches parent: K3=0.000560 (parent: 0.000560). The result is reproducible.
validity_notes: The frozen alpha=1.0 Laplace smoothing in the plug-in KL estimator creates a positive bias that exceeds the true CMI signal. With 12 target classes and average stratum size ~6, each (z,a) cell receives 12 pseudo-counts from smoothing, dominating the empirical counts. The degenerate control (K3=0.109 on deterministic SPA) quantifies this bias, which exceeds the stochastic SPA measurement (K3=0.099), making the estimator LESS sensitive on the positive control than on the degenerate baseline.

sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_classif with discrete_features=True appears to ignore the n_neighbors parameter for purely discrete data. K3 values for k=5, k=10, and k=20 are identical to 6 decimal places (0.000560). This is likely because the nearest-neighbor search for discrete data uses exact matching rather than distance-based neighborhoods, making k irrelevant when many samples tie on all features.

The per-stratum PMI (1.46-1.69 bits) detected by the exploratory permutation test is consistent with the parent audit's theoretical CMI of ~1.52 bits. This confirms the signal exists and is strong, but the frozen CMI estimators (KSG, plug-in KL with alpha=1.0) cannot detect it due to estimator-specific limitations.

Within-session shuffle (correcting parent's global shuffle deviation) was implemented. The C1 margin is 1.6-8x below threshold for plug-in KL and 8x for KSG, so the correction does not change C1 pass/fail.
All data is synthetic in-memory SPA simulation with N=5000 transitions (50 sessions x 100 steps, seed=42). No browser, network, or production SPA data.
The stratum size decomposition shows only 2 non-empty buckets (5-9, 10-19), with no 20-49 or 50+ strata. The high-dimensional conditioning (state, history_action_K=3) creates many small strata.
unresolved: Whether a smaller Laplace alpha (e.g., 0.1 or 0.01) would allow the plug-in KL estimator to detect the 1.52-bit signal. The frozen spec mandates alpha=1.0, which creates excessive smoothing bias.

Whether sklearn's mutual_info_classif with continuous_features (instead of discrete_features=True) would make the KSG k parameter effective on this discrete dataset. The current implementation appears to use categorical matching rather than distance-based neighborhoods.
Whether a non-smoothed plug-in estimator (maximum likelihood, no Laplace) would recover the true CMI. MLE would be noisy but unbiased for large strata.
Whether the CMI estimation failure is fundamental to discrete state spaces with high-dimensional conditioning, or specific to the estimator implementations tested.
Whether the per-stratum PMI signal (1.46-1.69 bits, all p=0.0) can be used as an alternative detection paradigm for beyond-Markov dynamics, bypassing CMI estimation entirely.
The generalization of these findings beyond 12-state discrete SPA to production Web transitions with continuous state representations.
